skills.name: Art History
skills.description: From handprints on cave walls to street art, and how to look closely at any work of art.
skills.masteryPromise: Walk through a major museum and understand much more of what you're looking at, and why it mattered.

skills.name: World Geography
skills.description: From reading a map to the mountains, rivers, climates and peoples of every continent.
skills.masteryPromise: Look at a map of any region and understand its land, climate, people and why they fit together.

skills.name: Ancient Rome
skills.description: From a village on the Tiber to an empire around the Mediterranean, and why it still shapes our laws, words and cities.
skills.masteryPromise: Explain how a village on the Tiber became an empire, how it worked, why it fell and what it left us.

skills.name: How Money Works
skills.description: From barter and coins to banks, markets, inflation and trade: the ideas behind every price you pay.
skills.masteryPromise: Understand the basics behind inflation, banks, debt, investing, markets and taxes, and follow money news.

skills.name: Astronomy
skills.description: From your cosmic address to the edge of the observable universe: the flagship 1–100 tree.
skills.masteryPromise: Follow mainstream astronomy news and understand the big ideas, from the planets to the Big Bang.

skills.name: Everyday Technology
skills.description: How the things around you actually work, from light bulbs and engines to phones, the internet and AI.
skills.masteryPromise: Explain how the everyday technology around you works, from the power grid to the phone in your hand.

skills.name: Music
skills.description: How sound becomes music, the instruments that make it, and the story from bone flutes to hip-hop.
skills.masteryPromise: Hear a piece from almost any era or place and know where it comes from and how it works.

skills.name: The Oceans
skills.description: Waves, tides, currents, the deep sea and the people who explore it: the ocean that covers most of Earth.
skills.masteryPromise: Understand how the ocean works, from tides and currents to the deep sea, and why it shapes life on land.

skills.name: The Middle Ages
skills.description: From Rome's fall in the West to the printing press: castles, crusades, plague and the wider medieval world.
skills.masteryPromise: Tell the story of the thousand years after Rome, and see through the usual myths about the Dark Ages.

skills.name: The Human Body
skills.description: From a single cell to bones, blood, brain and senses: how your body works and how to keep it working.
skills.masteryPromise: Understand how your body works, system by system, and make sense of what a doctor tells you.

skills.name: How Government Works
skills.description: Laws, rights, courts, elections and taxes: how people govern themselves and how you can take part.
skills.masteryPromise: Understand how governments, laws, courts and elections work, and follow the news with a clear head.

skills.name: Architecture
skills.description: Why buildings stand up and what they say about us, from pyramids and cathedrals to skyscrapers.
skills.masteryPromise: Look at almost any building, from a temple to a skyscraper, and see how it stands up and why it looks the way it does.

skills.name: Ancient Egypt
skills.description: Three thousand years on the Nile: pharaohs, pyramids, gods, hieroglyphs and how we rediscovered it all.
skills.masteryPromise: Tell the story of ancient Egypt from the Nile's first farmers to Cleopatra, and read a museum's Egypt room.

skills.name: The Animal Kingdom
skills.description: Mammals, birds, reptiles, sea life and insects: how animals live, survive, behave and evolve.
skills.masteryPromise: Understand how animals are built, how they survive and behave, and how evolution made them.

skills.name: Ancient Greece
skills.description: Myths, city-states, democracy, philosophy and Alexander: the Greek ideas the modern world still runs on.
skills.masteryPromise: Explain what the Greeks invented, from democracy to philosophy, and spot it in the world around you.

skills.name: Chemistry
skills.description: What everything is made of and how it changes: atoms, elements, reactions and the chemistry of daily life.
skills.masteryPromise: Understand what everything is made of, and explain the chemistry in your kitchen, your body and the news.

How art is kept, faked, stolen and remembered

skill.arts.music.title: How Music Works

skill.arts.music.title: Instruments

skill.arts.music.title: Early Music

Oldest complete song: the Seikilos epitaph
Notation moved music from memory to the page
From chant's one line to four voices, then print

skill.arts.music.title: Baroque and Classical

Classical: one clear melody, simplicity and clarity

Classical shaped the symphony and string quartet

skill.arts.music.title: The Romantic Century
learned: 1829: Mendelssohn revives Bach's St. Matthew Passion
Beethoven bridged Classical and Romantic
Chopin, Liszt, Verdi, Wagner, Tchaikovsky
Feeling first, and the past heard anew

skill.arts.music.title: Music Around the World
learned: Tala, gongan and bell phrase: music in cycles

Raga and maqam: modes with motifs, not just scales

skill.arts.music.title: Blues and Jazz
learned: Spirituals and work songs grew into the blues
Ragtime and blues fed New Orleans jazz
Armstrong made the solo central; swing filled dance floors

The Great Migration carried the music north

skill.arts.music.title: Rock and Pop
learned: Recording: from Scott's paper traces to Edison's playback

skill.arts.music.title: Hip-Hop, Electronic and Beyond

Synths and the 808 made notes and drums from circuits
Studios and computers reshaped voices and files
Streaming now brings in most recorded-music money

skill.arts.music.title: Music and You
learned: Sound, pitch, rhythm, melody, harmony and the staff
What music does in the brain, from chills to earworms
How scores steer films and games
Who gets paid, how to practice, and how to really listen

skill.geography.oceans.title: The Blue Planet
learned: All Earth's water: a ball about 1,385 km across
Warm water floats over the thermocline
Red fades first; no sunlight below 1,000 m
Pressure: about one atmosphere per 10 m
Salty all the way down: about 35 parts per thousand

skill.geography.oceans.title: The Ocean Floor
learned: Shelves appear first, by 140 m
Ridges at 2,000 to 3,000 m, with hot vents
Ooze blankets flat abyssal plains
Trenches hold the last water, down to about 11 km
Made at ridges, swallowed by trenches

skill.geography.oceans.title: Waves and Tides
learned: Tides are very long-period waves

Wind waves: speed, time and fetch; break at 1.3 times height

skill.geography.oceans.title: Currents and Climate
learned: Wind drives surface currents; Earth's spin bends them into gyres
The Gulf Stream carries heat north to Europe
Cold, salty water sinks into a 1,000-year conveyor
El Niño, hurricanes and heat all run through the ocean

skill.geography.oceans.title: The Sunlit Sea
learned: The ocean makes about half of Earth's oxygen
Food is made in roughly the top 5% of the water
Sunlight → phytoplankton, kelp, reef algae → everyone else
Sharks at the top keep the web in balance

skill.geography.oceans.title: The Deep
learned: Zones: sunlight, twilight, midnight, abyss, hadal
Pressure: be mostly water, with no air spaces
Dark: blue living light, or red bodies that vanish
Cold and hunger: wait, grow big, live on chemicals
Deepest fish ever filmed: 8,336 m

skill.geography.oceans.title: Coasts and Islands
learned: Sand: worn rock, shattered lava, shells and parrotfish
Waves quarry, grind and undercut, weak spots first
Estuaries, mangroves and drowned-valley harbors
Hot spot islands sink; reefs make atolls
Surtsey: built by fire, trimmed by waves

skill.geography.oceans.title: Polar Seas
learned: Arctic: ocean ringed by land; Antarctic: land ringed by ocean

Krill, whales and seals all live by the ice

skill.geography.oceans.title: Exploring the Ocean
learned: Polynesian voyagers settled the Pacific by about 1300 CE
Stars give latitude; clocks give longitude
Challenger proved the deep is alive
Scuba matches pressure; Trieste resisted it
1980: Nainoa Thompson sailed the old way home

skill.geography.oceans.title: People and the Ocean
learned: One salty, layered, mostly dark ocean
Fishing, farming and the limits of the catch
Ships, energy and pollution
Law, protection, pirates and legends

skill.geography.world_geography.title: Reading the Planet
learned: Your antipode is directly opposite, through Earth's center
Same latitude, other hemisphere, 180° of longitude away
Antipodes are about 12 hours apart
Most land is opposite ocean: the US faces the Indian Ocean

skill.geography.world_geography.title: The Restless Earth
learned: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and a hotspot
Plates there pull apart about 2 cm a year
Colliding plates build mountains and feed volcanoes
Sliding and sinking plates cause quakes and tsunamis

skill.geography.world_geography.title: Water World
learned: Total water stays constant; it only changes places
Ice-age glaciers lowered the sea about 120 m
Beringia linked Siberia and Alaska
Melting all Antarctic ice would raise the sea about 58 m

skill.geography.world_geography.title: Climate and Weather
learned: Sunlight lifts air at the Equator, where it rains
The dried air sinks near 30°, making deserts

George Hadley proposed the loop in 1735

skill.geography.world_geography.title: Biomes
learned: Earth runs on connected spheres: rock, water, air, life, ice
Mountains and air team up to make rain shadows
Climate sets the biome, on mountains and across latitudes
Half the tree done: onward to the regions of the world

skill.geography.world_geography.title: Africa and the Middle East
learned: The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and Red Seas

Ships skip the long trip around Africa

skill.geography.world_geography.title: Europe and Asia
learned: The Alpide belt runs from the Atlantic to Indonesia

Colliding continents crumple; subducting plates erupt

skill.geography.world_geography.title: The Americas
learned: The Pan-American Highway runs Alaska to Argentina

The Continental Divide follows the Rockies and the Andes
Mountains west, big rivers draining east, on both continents

skill.geography.world_geography.title: Oceania and the Poles
learned: The Arctic is ocean ringed by land; Antarctica is land ringed by ocean

Australia, the Pacific islands and both poles: mapped

skill.geography.world_geography.title: People and Places
learned: Maps, coordinates, time zones and GPS
Land, oceans and how to read them
Where people live, and the cities, borders and languages they share
Food, resources, migration and a changing planet

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: The Gift of the Nile
learned: Ethiopian rain made the Nile flood each year
Black land fed Egypt; the red desert guarded it
The Nile was a two-way road
Two lands became one kingdom around 3100 to 3000 BCE

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: Pharaohs and Power

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: The Pyramids

Built by paid, fed, rotating crews of Egyptians
Boats, sledges on wet sand and ramps moved the stone

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: Gods and the Afterlife
learned: Egyptians believed in many gods, pictured in many forms
Mummies kept a home for the ka and ba
Spells, amulets and shabtis prepared the dead

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: Writing and Knowledge

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: Daily Life
learned: Homes were mud brick; most towns vanished

Women had near-equal legal rights, not equal lives
Cats, senet and music filled daily life

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: The New Kingdom

Buffer zones grew into an empire

Akhenaten’s Aten revolution did not outlast him

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: Famous Pharaohs
learned: Khufu, Tutankhamun, Seti I, Ramesses II and Cleopatra in order

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: Decline and Conquest
learned: The Sea Peoples were beaten, but Egypt came out weaker
Kush, Persia, Alexander, the Ptolemies and Rome ruled in turn

skill.history.ancient_egypt.title: Rediscovering Egypt
learned: The Nile’s flood made the black land

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: Myth and Memory

Writing: Linear B, lost, then the alphabet

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: City-States

Acropolis and agora at every town’s heart
Citizens by birth; metics and slaves outside

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: Athens and Democracy

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: Sparta and War

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: Gods and Heroes

Heroes had hometowns: Athens, Mycenae, Tiryns
Athens kept a Feast of Union for Theseus

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: Thinkers
learned: Socrates taught Plato; Plato taught Aristotle

Aristotle observed and catalogued the world

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: Science and Math
learned: Archimedes put geometry on his grave

Measurement: Eratosthenes and Hipparchus
Argument: Hippocratic causes, Democritus’s atoms

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: Theater and the Arts

Art: contrapposto, red-figure, three orders

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: Alexander and After

skill.history.ancient_greece.title: The Greek Legacy
learned: From Bronze Age palaces to Homer and Troy
Myths tested against archaeology
Greek words, votes, columns and Games today

skill.history.ancient_rome.title: Founding and the Kings

skill.history.ancient_rome.title: The Early Republic

skill.history.ancient_rome.title: The Republic in Crisis

skill.history.ancient_rome.title: Augustus and the New Empire

skill.history.ancient_rome.title: Emperors Good and Bad

skill.history.ancient_rome.title: Life in the Roman World

skill.history.ancient_rome.title: How Rome Held an Empire

skill.history.ancient_rome.title: Crisis, Christianity and Division

skill.money.how_money_works.title: Big Ideas in Economics
learned: What money is and why people trust it

Big thinkers: Smith, Marx, Keynes, Hayek

skill.science.animals.title: What Makes an Animal

Blue whale to fairyfly: one kingdom, huge range

skill.science.animals.title: Animal Behavior
learned: Instinct, learning, and imprinting between them

skill.science.animals.title: Evolution

skill.science.animals.title: Animals and People
learned: What makes an animal, and how to sort one

How people tamed and farmed animals
Species threatened, lost and saved

skill.science.astronomy.title: Your Place in the Universe

skill.science.astronomy.title: The Sky Above You

skill.science.astronomy.title: The Sun and the Solar System’s Edge

skill.science.astronomy.title: Galaxies

skill.science.astronomy.title: The Universe

skill.science.chemistry.title: The Periodic Table

skill.science.human_body.title: The Building Blocks
learned: 11 organ systems, built from organs, tissues and cells
About 30 trillion human cells, roughly matched by bacteria
DNA sits mostly in the nucleus; genes are recipes for proteins
Water is 50 to 60% of an adult, mostly inside your cells
About 330 billion cells are replaced every day

skill.science.human_body.title: Bones and Muscles
learned: Adults have 206 bones; babies start with roughly 270 to 300
Bone is living tissue with blood-making marrow
Joints are fulcrums; bones are levers; muscles pull
Muscles only pull, so they work in pairs
Tendons link muscle to bone; ligaments link bone to bone

skill.science.human_body.title: Heart and Blood
learned: Four chambers, two pumps, one-way valves
Arteries out, veins back, capillaries deliver
Plasma, red cells, white cells and platelets
Blood types, blood pressure and clotting
Your blood laps your body about once a minute

skill.science.human_body.title: Breathing
learned: The nose warms, moistens and filters air
Down the bronchial tree to 480 million air sacs
Oxygen to the cells, carbon dioxide back out
Carbon dioxide drives the urge to breathe
Smoking damages airways and air sacs; asthma narrows airways

skill.science.human_body.title: Food and Digestion
learned: Food travels one tube and is absorbed in the small intestine
Absorbed sugars pass the liver, then reach every cell
Mitochondria combine fuel with oxygen to release energy
Blood carries both, delivered by one cardiovascular system

skill.science.human_body.title: Brain and Nerves
learned: Brain and spinal cord decide; nerves carry news in and orders out
Neurons: electrical along the axon, chemical across the synapse
Reflexes loop through the spinal cord before you feel the pain
Hippocampus files memories; sleep stages cycle through the night
The brain: about 2% of your weight, about 20% of your energy

skill.science.human_body.title: The Senses
learned: More than five senses: how many depends on how you count
Eyes focus light; the brain builds, flips and fills in the picture
Ears sort sound by pitch and keep you balanced
Flavor is taste plus smell; skin senses touch, heat and pain
Receptors sense; the brain perceives, and tunes out what doesn't change

skill.science.human_body.title: Defending the Body
learned: Skin is the wall: dead cells, dry and acidic
Innate immunity: phagocytes and fever
Acquired immunity: antibodies, B and T cells, memory
Human tools: handwashing, vaccines, penicillin
Lymph nodes are where white blood cells meet germs

skill.science.human_body.title: Growing and Changing
learned: Egg and sperm make one cell; it becomes a fetus at week 10
Traits pass down in allele pairs; most involve many genes
A hormone relay starts puberty; the brain matures last
Telomeres, senescent cells and damage drive aging
Epigenetic tags let time edit how genes are used

skill.science.human_body.title: Keeping Healthy
learned: From 30 trillion cells to 11 organ systems
DNA, genes and the proteins they build
Diet, movement, sleep and stress
How medicine is tested, and how myths are busted

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: Energy and Electricity
learned: Generators make electricity; batteries store energy as chemicals

A watt is a joule per second: volts times amps
A kilowatt-hour is 3.6 million joules

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: Power for the World
learned: Coal and renewables each made about a third of 2025's power
Most sources spin a turbine; solar panels don't
Fuel, atoms and nature each trade off carbon, waste and weather
The grid steps power up, carries it, and steps it down

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: Engines and Motion
learned: One horsepower is about 746 watts
Engines turn heat into motion; motors turn electricity into motion
Simple machines, gears and hydraulics trade force for distance
No machine creates energy

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: Getting Around
learned: Wings, jets, propellers and rockets all throw something backward

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: Communication
learned: Chapter 1 used electricity for power; Chapter 5 used it for messages

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: Computers
learned: A key press runs through binary, RAM, software, transistors and pixels

Binary, memory and a programmable design make a computer

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: The Internet
learned: Wi-Fi radio carries your message to the router; then it travels as packets

Light in fiber takes about 5 millionths of a second per kilometer

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: Home and Health
learned: Fridges, air conditioners and heat pumps all move heat
Water and sewage plants filter, settle and disinfect

Pasteur and Koch named the enemy that vaccines and antibiotics fight

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: Building and Making

Assembly lines, robots and 3D printers changed how things are made

skill.world_systems.everyday_technology.title: Tomorrow's Technology
learned: From stone tools to the power grid
Electricity made, stored and used
AI, chatbots, VR and drones, explained
Gene editing, fusion and quantum computing, without the hype

skill.world_systems.government.title: Why Government?
learned: Humans are political animals, said Aristotle
Rules and laws let everyone play the same game
Authority is power people accept

skill.world_systems.government.title: Kinds of Government

skill.world_systems.government.title: Democracy

skill.world_systems.government.title: Money and Government

learned: The Antarctic Treaty froze claims by agreement

skill.world_systems.government.title: You and Government

Citizenship, rights and responsibilities
